At this time, the city expanded and new projects of infrastructures started coming up. As a result of the expansion, there was an appreciation of real estate prices at the rate of 50%. Next two years the land's value appreciation is 50%, after 2 years

So, after two years of appreciation, the value of the land is, ⇒ 243000/4 × 9 = 546750

questions.question: A shopkeeper marks up the price of the oil by 40% and uses a faulty machine which measures 15% less. If the shopkeeper gives a discount of 32%, the profit/loss percentage is:
questions.questionHtml: A shopkeeper marks up the price of the oil by 40% and uses a faulty machine which measures 15% less. If the shopkeeper gives a discount of 32%, the profit/loss percentage is:
questions.solution:
CP = 100, Marked Price (MP) = 140

Faulty machine measures 15% less, so quantity sold = 85% of CP

Discount = 32% of MP = 0.32 × 140 = 44.8

SP after discount = 140 - 44.8 = 95.2

Effective quantity sold = 85% of 100 = 85

Profit = SP - Effective CP = 95.2 - 85 = 10.2

Profit percentage = (10.2 / 85) × 100 = 12%

questions.question: If half of the quantity of sugar in a bag was sold at a profit of 20%, a quarter of the quantity of sugar in the bag was sold at a profit of 16%, and the remaining sugar in the bag was sold at a profit of 24%, and the total profit obtained by selling all the sugar in the bag was Rs. 90, what was the cost price of the entire quantity of sugar in the bag?
questions.questionHtml: If half of the quantity of sugar in a bag was sold at a profit of 20%, a quarter of the quantity of sugar in the bag was sold at a profit of 16%, and the remaining sugar in the bag was sold at a profit of 24%, and the total profit obtained by selling all the sugar in the bag was Rs. 90, what was the cost price of the entire quantity of sugar in the bag?
questions.solution:
Let the cost price of sugar be Rs. x per Kg

Suppose there is 200 kg of sugar in the bag, then total price of the sugar in the bag = 200 × x = 200x

The profit on 100 kg of sugar = 20%

The profit on 50 kg of sugar = 16% [quarter of the quantity of the sugar, \(\frac{1}{4}\times 200 \)]

The profit on 50 kg of sugar = 24% [Left amount is 50 kg]

Total profit on cost price = Rs. 90

⇒\(\frac{20}{100}\times100x \) + \(\frac{16}{100}\times 50x \) + \(\frac{24}{100}\times 50x \) = 90 ⇒ 20x + 8x + 12x = 90 ⇒ x = \(\frac{9}{4}\)

The Cost price of sugar = 200x = 200 × \(\frac{9}{4}\) = 450

questions.question: Sukhvir purchased some perishable items for sale but 30% of those items could not be sold and went bad. However, Sukhvir managed to sell the rest of the items at a price that helped him earn an overall profit of 19%. At what percentage above the cost price of each item purchased by Sukhvir did he sell each of the items that did not go bad?
questions.questionHtml: Sukhvir purchased some perishable items for sale but 30% of those items could not be sold and went bad. However, Sukhvir managed to sell the rest of the items at a price that helped him earn an overall profit of 19%. At what percentage above the cost price of each item purchased by Sukhvir did he sell each of the items that did not go bad?
questions.solution:
Let the total number of items be 100 and the cost price of each item be Rs 100

Total CP = 100 × 100 = Rs 10000

Total SP = 10000 × (100 + 19) /100 = Rs11900

Number of good items = (100 - 30) = 70

SP of each good items = 11900 / 70 = Rs 170

So, profit percentage on each good item = 170 - 100 = 70

questions.question: The profit earned after selling an article for Rs.8,579 is the same as the loss incurred after selling the article for Rs.6,341. The profit percentage is:
questions.questionHtml: The profit earned after selling an article for Rs.8,579 is the same as the loss incurred after selling the article for Rs.6,341. The profit percentage is:
questions.solution:
Given:

SP1 = Rs.8579 

SP2 = Rs.6341

Formulas used:

Profit = Selling price - Cost price

Loss = Cost price - Selling price 

Profit percent = Profit/Cost price × 100

Calculation:

Let the profit be = Rs.x 

CP1 = CP2

⇒ Rs.8579 - x = x + Rs.6341 

⇒ 8579 - 6341 = 2x 

⇒ x = 2238/2  

⇒ Profit = Rs.1119

⇒ Cost price = 8579 - 1119

⇒ Rs.7460

Profit percent = 1119/7460 × 100 

⇒ 15%

∴ The required profit percent = 15%

Shortcut Trick When profit or loss is equal:

 Cost price = (SP1 + SP2)/2

⇒ (Rs.8579 + Rs.6341)/2 = Rs.7460

⇒ Loss = Rs.7460 - Rs.6341

⇒ Rs.1119 

Profit % = 1119/7460 × 100 = 15%

questions.question: Amit earns a profit of 24% by selling an article for ₹167.40. By how much (in ₹) should he increase the selling price of the article to get a profit of 38%?
questions.questionHtml: Amit earns a profit of 24% by selling an article for ₹167.40. By how much (in ₹) should he increase the selling price of the article to get a profit of 38%?
questions.solution:
Formula:

\(SP_1\over 100+G_1\) = \(SP_2\over 100+G_2\), where

SP1 and SP2 are the selling prices respectively.

G1 and G2 are the gain % on selling prices SP1 and SP2 respectively. 

Calculation:

Substituting the values, we get-

⇒\(167.4\over 100+24\) = \(SP_2\over 100+38\)

⇒ SP2 = 167.4 × \(138\over 124\) = Rs 186.3

Difference = Rs 186.3 - Rs 167.40 = Rs 18.9

∴ The increase in selling price is Rs 18.9.

questions.question: A trader earns 29% profit by selling an article. If he increases the selling price by ₹ 90, his gain per cent increases to 37%. What is the selling price (in ₹) of the article, if he sells it at 20% profit?
questions.questionHtml: A trader earns 29% profit by selling an article. If he increases the selling price by ₹ 90, his gain per cent increases to 37%. What is the selling price (in ₹) of the article, if he sells it at 20% profit?
questions.solution:
Given:

first profit earn = 29%

SP increases by ₹90

Concept Used:

SP = CP x (100 + profit%)/100

Calculation:

Let CP be 100Rs

Increase in profit in % = 37% - 29% = 8%

8% = 90 rupees

1 % = 90/8

100% = (90/8) x 100 = 1125

CP = 1125

SP after 20% profit = CP x (100 + profit%)/100

= 1125 x (120/100)

=  ₹1350 

Therefore, SP after 20% profit is  ₹1350.

questions.question: Suhani pays tax at the rate of 30% on her entire income of Rs. 90,000 and Ritika pays tax at the rate of 40% on her entire income of Rs. y. If the overall tax rate on their combined income comes to 37%, then what is the value of y?

questions.solution: (90000 × 30%) + (y × 40%) = (90000 + y) × 37% ⇒ 27000 + y × 40% = 33,300 + y × 37% ⇒ y × 3% = 6300 ⇒ y = (6300 × 100)/3 ⇒ y = 210000

Cost of each item = total cost/number of items

⇒ x = 800/4

⇒ x = 200

444 - a = \(1\over5 \) ×( a - 390) ⇒ 2220 - 5a = a - 390 ⇒ a = \(2610\over6\) = Rs 435

Profit = Rs 522 - Rs 435 = Rs 87 and Profit % = \(87\over435\) × 100 = 20%

questions.question: Ramesh purchases a table and a chair for Rs. 3,900. He sells the table at a profit of 8% and the chair at a profit of 16%. He earns a profit of Rs. 540. What is the difference between the original price of the table and the chair?
questions.questionHtml: Ramesh purchases a table and a chair for Rs. 3,900. He sells the table at a profit of 8% and the chair at a profit of 16%. He earns a profit of Rs. 540. What is the difference between the original price of the table and the chair?
questions.solution:
Let the original price of the chair be Rs. Q, then original price of the table = Rs. (3900 - Q)

According to the question, Q × 16% + (3900 - Q) × 8% = 540

⇒ 16Q + 3900 × 8 - 8Q = 54000 ⇒ 8Q = 54000 - 3900 × 8n ⇒ 8Q = 22800 ⇒ Q = 2850

So, the original price of the table = 3900 - 2850 = Rs. 1050

Now, the price difference between the chair and table = 2850 - 1050 = Rs. 1800

questions.question: A watch is sold at a profit of 25%. If both the cost price and the selling price of the watch are decreased by Rs. 75, then the profit would be 30%. The original selling price (in Rs.) of the watch is:
questions.questionHtml: A watch is sold at a profit of 25%. If both the cost price and the selling price of the watch are decreased by Rs. 75, then the profit would be 30%. The original selling price (in Rs.) of the watch is:
questions.solution:
Formula:

SP = CP + (\(G\over 100\) × CP), where

SP = Selling Price

CP = Cost Price

G = Gain%

Gain = SP - CP

Calculation:

Let the watch cost price be a.

SP = a + (\(25\over 100\) × a) = a + \(a\over 4\) = \(5a\over 4\)

New cost price = a - 75

New SP = 1.3 × (a - 75)

According to the question-

⇒ 1.3 × (a - 75) = \(5\over4\)a - 75

⇒ 5.2 × (a - 75) = 5a - 300

⇒ 5.2a - 390 = 5a - 300

⇒ 0.2a = 90

⇒ a = \(90\over0.2\) = 450

Original selling price = \(5\over4\) × 450 = Rs 562.5

∴ The original selling price is Rs 562.5.

questions.question: A bought 38 kg rice @ Rs. 54.50/kg, 45 kg rice @ Rs. 62/kg and 55 kg rice @ Rs. 48/kg. He sold the mixture @ Rs. 65/kg. His profit or loss percentage is∶
questions.questionHtml: A bought 38 kg rice @ Rs. 54.50/kg, 45 kg rice @ Rs. 62/kg and 55 kg rice @ Rs. 48/kg. He sold the mixture @ Rs. 65/kg. His profit or loss percentage is∶
questions.solution:
Cost price of 38 kg rice at the rate of Rs. 54.50/kg = 38 × 54.5 = 38 × 109/2 = 19 × 109

= Rs. 2071

Cost price of 45 kg rice at the rate of Rs. 62/kg = 45 × 62 = 90/2 × 62 = 90 × 31 = Rs. 2790

Cost price of 55 kg rice at the rate of Rs. 48/kg = 55 × 48 = 110/2 × 48 = 110 × 24 = Rs. 2640

Total cost price = 2071 + 2790 + 2640 = Rs. 7501

Total quantity of mixture = 38 + 45 + 55 = 138 kg

Selling price of the mixture = Rs. 65/kg

Total selling price = 138 × 65 = Rs. 8970

Profit percentage = (8970 – 7501)/7501 × 100 = 19.58% ≈ 19.6%

questions.question: The cost prices of articles A and B are the same. A is sold at 20% profit, whereas B is sold for Rs. 54.60 more than the selling price of A. If the overall profit earned on selling A and B is 28%, then what is the cost price of each article?
questions.questionHtml: The cost prices of articles A and B are the same. A is sold at 20% profit, whereas B is sold for Rs. 54.60 more than the selling price of A. If the overall profit earned on selling A and B is 28%, then what is the cost price of each article?
questions.solution:
Given:

A is sold at 20% profit, B is sold for Rs. 54.60 more than the selling price of A

The overall profit earned on selling A and B is 28%

Formula used:

Profit = Selling price – Cost price

SP = [(100 + profit %)/100 × CP]

Calculation:

Let C.P of A nd B be Rs. x

According to the question:

S.P of A = (x × 120/100) = 6x/5

S.P of B = (6x/5 + 54.60)

Total C.P = Rs. (x + x) = Rs. 2x

Total S.P = (6x/5 + 54.60 + 6x/5)

⇒ (12x/5 + 54.60)

Profit = (12x/5 + 54.60 – 2x)

⇒ 2x/5 + 54.60

Now,

⇒ 28% of 2x = 2x/5 + 54.60

⇒ [(28/100) × 2x] = 2x/5 + 54.60

⇒ [(28/100) × 2x] = [2x/5 + (5460/100)]

⇒ [(28/100) × 2x] = (4x + 546)/10

⇒ 28x = 20x + 2730

⇒ 8x = 2730

⇒ x = 2730/8 = Rs. 341.25

∴The cost price of each article is Rs. 341.25.

⇒ SP = 1040/26 = 40

Now, SP of 5 kg of sugar = 40 × 5 = Rs. 200

questions.question: The selling price of a book, including the sales tax, is Rs.956.34. The rate of sales tax is 10%. If the shopkeeper has made a profit of 15%. then the cost price of the book is:
questions.questionHtml: The selling price of a book, including the sales tax, is Rs.956.34. The rate of sales tax is 10%. If the shopkeeper has made a profit of 15%. then the cost price of the book is:
questions.solution:
Given:

The selling price of a book, including the sales tax, is Rs.956.34

The rate of sales tax is 10%.

The shopkeeper made a profit of 15%.

Calculation:

Let the actual selling price be x

⇒ x + 10% x = 956.34

⇒ x + 10(x)/100 = 956.34

⇒ x + x/10 = 956.34

⇒ 11x/10 = 956.34

⇒ x = (956.34 × 10)/11

⇒ x = 869.4

Now let CP be 100

⇒ Profit % = 15%

⇒ SP = 100 × 115/100

⇒ SP = 115

⇒ 115 = 869.4

⇒ 1 = 869.4/115

⇒ CP = 100 × 869.4/115

⇒ CP = 756

∴ The cost price of a book is Rs.756.

Shortcut TrickCP = \(\frac{SP}{(1 \space + \space Sales \space tax) \space (1 \space + \space Profit)} \)

CP = \(\frac{956.34}{(1 \space + \space .10) \space (1 \space + \space .15)} \)

CP = 756

questions.question: The cost price of articles X and Y is the same. Article X is sold at 20% profit and article Y is sold for Rs. 126 less than the selling price of X. If the net profit by selling both the articles is 14%, then what is the cost price (in Rs.) of each article?
questions.questionHtml: The cost price of articles X and Y is the same. Article X is sold at 20% profit and article Y is sold for Rs. 126 less than the selling price of X. If the net profit by selling both the articles is 14%, then what is the cost price (in Rs.) of each article?
questions.solution:
Given:

The article X sold at = 20% profit

Formula used:

P = SP - CP     Where, P = Profit, SP = Selling price, and CP = Cost price

Calculation:

Let the cost price of the articles be C

According to the question

The selling price of the X = 1.2C

The selling price of the Y = 1.2C - 126

The cost price of both articles = 2C

⇒ \({14\over 100}\ =\ {{(1.2C\ +\ 1.2C\ -\ 126)}\ -\ 2C\over 2C}\)

⇒ \({14\over 50}\ =\ {{(2.4C\ -\ 126)}\ -\ 2C\over C}\)

⇒ \({7\over 25}\ =\ {2.4C\ -\ 126\ -\ 2C\over C}\)

⇒ \({7\over 25}\ =\ {0.4C\ -\ 126\over C}\)

⇒ 7C = 10C - 3150

⇒ 3C = 3150

The cost price of each article = C = 1050

∴ The required result will be 1050.

questions.question: A sells an article to B at 20% profit. B sells it to C at 15% loss. C sells it to D at 25% profit. If the difference between the profit of A and C is ₹ 132 and B bought the article for ₹ x, then what is the value of x?
questions.questionHtml: A sells an article to B at 20% profit. B sells it to C at 15% loss. C sells it to D at 25% profit. If the difference between the profit of A and C is ₹ 132 and B bought the article for ₹ x, then what is the value of x?
questions.solution:
Given:

A sells an article to B at 20% profit. B sells it to C at 15% loss. C sells it to D at 25% profit.

The difference between the profit of A and C is ₹ 132

Concept used:

Selling Price = Cost Price + Cost Price × Profit%

Selling Price = Cost Price - Cost Price × Loss%

Calculation:

Let the cost price of the article in case of A be Rs. 100Q.

Hence,

Cost-price of B = 100Q + 100Q × 20% = Rs. 120Q

Cost-price of C = 120Q - 120Q × 15% = Rs. 102Q

Cost-price of D = 102Q + 102Q × 25% = Rs. 127.5Q

According to the question,

(127.5Q - 102Q) - (120Q - 100Q) = 132 (Taking the positive difference)

⇒ 25.5Q - 20Q = 132

⇒ Q = 24

Hence, Cost-price of B = 120 × 24 = Rs. 2880 

∴ The value of x is Rs. 2880.

questions.question: A shopkeeper announced a 30% discount on the marked price of an item. A person bought the item from the shop for Rs. 21,000 after getting the discount, and sold the item to a customer in such a way that he earned a profit of 32% on the marked price. What is the profit (in Rs.) the person earned by selling the item?
questions.questionHtml: A shopkeeper announced a 30% discount on the marked price of an item. A person bought the item from the shop for Rs. 21,000 after getting the discount, and sold the item to a customer in such a way that he earned a profit of 32% on the marked price. What is the profit (in Rs.) the person earned by selling the item?
questions.solution:
Given:

Shopkeeper offered 30% discount.

Selling price for shopkeeper is Rs. 21,000

A person sold at 32% profit on MP

Concept Used:

%Discount = (MP – SP)/MP × 100

% Profit = (SP – CP)/CP × 100

Calculation:

Shopkeeper sold for Rs. 21,000 at 30% discount

Let the Marked price of a item be x

He gave 30% on MP

⇒ Selling price = (100 – 30)% of x

⇒ 70% of x = 21,000

⇒ (70/100) × x = 21,000

⇒ x = 30,000

Marked price of an item is 30,000

Now the person sold the item at 32% profit on MP.

Selling price for the person is,

⇒ (100 + 32)% of MP

⇒ 132% × 30,000

⇒ (132/100) × 30,000

⇒ 39,600 

Selling price of an item for the person is Rs. 39,600

Now profit of the person,

⇒ Selling price  – Cost/Purchased price

⇒ 39,600  – 21,000

⇒ 18,600

∴ The profit of a person is Rs. 18,600.

questions.question: The difference between the selling prices of some articles if sold for Rs. 12 per article instead of Rs. 9 per article is Rs. 150. If the cost price of these articles is Rs. 250, then find the selling price of 21 articles if profit earned is 20%.
questions.questionHtml: The difference between the selling prices of some articles if sold for Rs. 12 per article instead of Rs. 9 per article is Rs. 150. If the cost price of these articles is Rs. 250, then find the selling price of 21 articles if profit earned is 20%.
questions.solution:
Given:

The difference between the selling prices of some articles if sold for Rs. 12 per article instead of Rs. 9 per article is Rs. 150

Total cost price = Rs. 250

Formula Used:

Cost price per article = Total cost price/Number of article

Selling price = Number of article × Cost price × (100 + profit %)/100

Calculation:

Let the number of article be x.

Selling price at Rs. 12 per article – Selling price at Rs. 9 per article = 150

⇒ 12x – 9x = 150

⇒ 3x = 150

⇒ x = 50

Cost price per article = Total cost price/Number of article

⇒ 250/50

⇒ Rs. 5

Selling price = Number of article × Cost price × (100 + profit %)/100

⇒ 21 × 5 × (100 + 20)/100

⇒ 105 × 120/100

⇒ 126

∴ The selling price of 21 articles with 20% profit is Rs. 126.

questions.question: On selling an article for ₹246.80, the gain is 20% more than the amount of loss incurred on selling it for ₹216. If the article is sold for ₹320.75, then what is the percentage (correct to one decimal place) profit/loss?
questions.questionHtml: On selling an article for ₹246.80, the gain is 20% more than the amount of loss incurred on selling it for ₹216. If the article is sold for ₹320.75, then what is the percentage (correct to one decimal place) profit/loss?
questions.solution:
Formula:

P% = \(\frac{(SP - CP)}{CP} \times 100\),

L = CP - SP

P = SP - CP, where

P% = Profit %

SP = Selling Price

CP = Cost Price

L = Loss

P = Profit

Calculation:

Let the amount at which the article is sold be "a".

According to the question-

⇒ 246.8 - a = 1.2 × (a - 216)

⇒ 246.8 - a = 1.2a - 259.2

⇒ 2.2a = ₹506

⇒ a = ₹230

Profit when sold for ₹320.75 = ₹320.75 - ₹230 = ₹90.75

questions.question: A person sold an article at a loss of 12%. Had he sold it at a gain of 10.5%, he would have got Rs. 112.50 more. What is the original selling price (in Rs.) of the article?
questions.questionHtml: A person sold an article at a loss of 12%. Had he sold it at a gain of 10.5%, he would have got Rs. 112.50 more. What is the original selling price (in Rs.) of the article?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total percentage gap = Loss% + Gain% = 12% + 10.5% = 22.5%

According to the question, 22.5% of Cost Price (CP) = ₹112.50

⇒ 1% of CP = 112.50 ÷ 22.5 = ₹5

Original Selling Price = CP − 12% Loss = 88% of CP

⇒ 88% = 88 × 5 = ₹440

∴ The correct answer is ₹440.00.

Alternate Method

Given:

Initial loss = 12%

New gain = 10.5%

Difference in Selling Price (SP) = ₹112.50

Formula Used:

SP = CP × (100 ± Profit/Loss%) ÷ 100

Calculations:

⇒ Let the Cost Price of the article be ₹x.

⇒ Original Selling Price (SP1) = x × (100 − 12) ÷ 100 = 0.88x

⇒ New Selling Price (SP2) = x × (100 + 10.5) ÷ 100 = 1.105x

⇒ Difference = SP2 − SP1

⇒ 1.105x − 0.88x = 112.50

⇒ 0.225x = 112.50

⇒ x = 112.50 ÷ 0.225 = ₹500

⇒ Original Selling Price = 0.88 × 500

⇒ Original Selling Price = ₹440

∴ The correct answer is ₹440.00.

Additional Information

Profit and Loss Percentage

Profit% = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100 and Loss% = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100. Both are always calculated on the Cost Price unless stated otherwise.

Successive Percentage Changes

If an object is sold through multiple hands at profits a% and b%, the net profit is given by [a + b + (ab ÷ 100)]%.

Marked Price and Discount

Selling Price = Marked Price (MP) − Discount. Discount is usually calculated as a percentage of the MP.

Profit and Loss

Calculation:

A shopkeeper has 76 articles so,

20 articles are sold at profit of 15%

⇒ \(20 × \frac{{115}}{{100}} = Rs.23\)

40 articles are sold at 19% 

⇒ \(40 × \frac{{119}}{{100}} = Rs.47.6\)

Remaining 16 articles are sold at 25% profit

⇒ \(16 × \frac{{125}}{{100}} = Rs.20\)

Total selling price = 23 + 20 + 47.6 

Total selling price = 90.60 × 100 = Rs.9060

Profit = 9060 - 7600 = 1460

As per the question,

⇒ 1460 unit = 27740

⇒ 100 unit = \(\frac{{27740}}{{1460}} \times 100\)

∴ CP of one article = Rs1900

questions.question: A man buys goods for Rs. 8,000. He sells 30% of those goods at a profit of 12% and 40% of the remaining goods at a profit of 25%. At what profit percentage should he sell the remaining goods to gain 30% in the entire transaction (correct to one decimal place)?
questions.questionHtml: A man buys goods for Rs. 8,000. He sells 30% of those goods at a profit of 12% and 40% of the remaining goods at a profit of 25%. At what profit percentage should he sell the remaining goods to gain 30% in the entire transaction (correct to one decimal place)?
questions.solution:
Given:

Cost price of goods = Rs. 8000

Formula used:

Profit = SP – CP

Profit% = Profit/CP × 100

Calculation:

According to the question

30%of goods = (8000 × 30/100)

⇒ Rs. 2400

Profit = 12%

SP = (2400 × 112/100)

⇒ Rs. 2688

CP of 40% of remaining goods = (8000 – 2400) = Rs. 5600

⇒ (5600 × 40/100)

⇒ Rs. 2240

CP of 40% of remaining goods = Rs. 2240

Profit = 25%

SP = (2240 × 125/100)

⇒ Rs. 2800

He has to gain 30% on whole transaction

SP = (8000 × 130/100)

⇒ Rs. 10400

CP left = [8000 – (2400 + 2240)

⇒ (8000 – 4640)

⇒ Rs. 3360

SP left = [10400 – (2688 + 2800)]

⇒ (10400 – 5488)

⇒ Rs. 4912

Profit ended on remaining goods = Rs. (4912 – 3360)

⇒ Rs. 1552

Profit% = (1552/3360 × 100)

⇒ Rs.(155,200/3360)

⇒ 46.2%

∴ Required profit percentage is 46.2%

questions.question: On selling a television at a 6% profit and a fridge at a 9% profit, a shopkeeper gains Rs. 5,100. However, if the shopkeeper sells the television at a 9% profit and the fridge at a 6% loss, he gains Rs. 1,800 on the whole transaction. The cost price (in Rs.) of the fridge is:

CP(1 + P/100) = SP

Calculation

⇒ 13y = 390000

⇒ y = 30000
